analysis:
MARKET & PORTFOLIO OVERVIEW: SPY is in a confirmed uptrend (+2.0% vs SMA50, positive 20d slope), providing a permissive backdrop for long exposure. The portfolio is deployed at 52% equity across 4 positions. However, the track record demands humility: a 9.1% win rate and 0.03x profit factor signal that sizing discipline and selectivity are more important than activity right now.

EXISTING POSITION REVIEW:
- AMP (-6.35%): Most concerning holding. We have been stopped out of AMP TWICE previously (-3.12%, -3.81%), and the third attempt is now -6.35%. The pattern of repeated entries into a losing name is a behavioral red flag. AMP does not appear in today's screened candidate list, which may indicate trend deterioration. If this position breaks below its stop, do NOT re-enter a fourth time without a materially different setup.
- BR (-3.30%) and MCO (-0.25%): Both underwater but within tolerable ranges. However, AMP + BR + MCO represents 3 financial-sector positions, all in the red simultaneously. This is over-concentration in a single sector. No fresh capital should go toward adding more financial exposure.
- NVDA (+4.91%): The only winner; confirmed uptrend, strong fundamentals, appears on today's screened list. Thesis intact — hold.

NEW TRADE RATIONALE: With 4 positions already open (top of the 3-5 range) and a struggling track record, the bar for a new entry is high. One setup clears it: TEL (TE Connectivity) is basing at only 30% of its 52-week range with SMA50 slope just turning positive — the textbook Stage 1→2 Weinstein transition this strategy was designed to exploit. Valuation is reasonable (fwd PEG 0.90, fwd P/E 16.5) and quality metrics are solid. No other candidates are compelling enough to add a 6th position against our current track record. Cash remains the preferred default for remaining headroom if TEL entry is not confirmed.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $210.00 or better. Prefer entry on a minor intraday pullback toward $207-208 (closer to SMA50). Do not chase above $213. Confirm the basing zone above $200 remains intact before executing.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: TE Connectivity is a high-quality industrial-technology connector business with a 23.3% ROE, 20.8% operating margin, $2.3B FCF, and 13.8% revenue growth. Forward PEG of 0.90 and fwd P/E of 16.5x represent fair value for this quality profile. EPS revisions are modestly positive. The business has durable exposure to automotive electrification, industrial automation, and data infrastructure — secular growth vectors. TECHNICAL: At 30% of its 52-week range ($194-$246), TEL is in the lower half of its range — the preferred basing zone for this strategy. Price is only +1.7% above SMA50, and the SMA50 slope has just turned marginally positive (+0.3%) after being flat, signaling a potential Stage 1 to Stage 2 transition. This is exactly the entry profile the strategy targets: quality at fair value when the trend has stopped going down. Stop at 1.5x ATR ($9.46 below entry at $200.55) defines clear risk with a 4.5% stop, well within rules. Position sized to 113 shares ($23,731) — capped at 25% of equity — with worst-case risk of ~$1,069 (1.12% of portfolio heat).
trades.exit_plan: PRIMARY STOP: $200.55 on a daily close below (1.5x ATR). THESIS BREAK: Exit immediately if TEL closes below $194 (52-week low broken) or if SMA50 rolls over with price below it for two consecutive weeks. EARNINGS RISK: Earnings are Oct 28 (35 days). If the position is profitable heading into earnings, consider trimming 50% before the report to reduce binary risk. TIME STOP: If TEL has not made progress toward $220 within 8 weeks, reassess momentum. PROFIT TRAIL: If price exceeds $225, trail stop to breakeven; if it reaches $230, trail stop to $218 to lock in partial gain.
